extracted.intended_audience: postdoctoral researchers (and sponsoring institutions/mentors) preparing K99/R00 Pathway to Independence applications
extracted.subtask_description: Prepare and submit a K99/R00 NIH Pathway to Independence (Parent K99/R00 — Independent Clinical Trial Not Allowed) application, including mentored K99 and planned R00 independent phases, meeting NIH programmatic, budgetary, eligibility, and institutional requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and expected transition timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: The K99/R00 award is intended to facilitate a timely transition of postdoctoral researchers to independent, tenure-track or equivalent faculty positions by providing up to 2 years mentored (K99) support and up to 3 years independent (R00) support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strong candidates will require and propose a well-conceived plan for 1–2 years of substantive mentored research and career development. The two award phases are intended to be continuous in time; exceptions are rare. An individual who cannot provide a compelling rationale for at least one year of additional mentored research/career development is not a strong candidate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — postdoctoral experience limit
rubrics_metrics.description: K99/R00 applicants must have no more than 4 years of postdoctoral research experience as of the application due date (new or resubmission).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only time dedicated to research counts toward the 4-year limit; part-time research is pro-rated. One-year extension approved for childbirth (see NIH Extension Policy for Early Stage Investigator Status); other parental, medical, military, or well-justified leaves typically are not counted if generally less than 12 months. Candidates are strongly encouraged to confirm eligibility with the relevant IC and to document exceptional situations with Program Contacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — current appointment type (must be mentored postdoctoral)
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals must be in mentored, postdoctoral training positions to be eligible; if a candidate achieves independence (any faculty or non-mentored research position) before a K99 award is made, neither the K99 nor the R00 will be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a position title is non-standard, the candidate should provide institutional documentation (e.g., published position description) demonstrating that the position is a mentored postdoctoral training position. Clinicians in clinical faculty positions that denote independence in clinical responsibilities but not in research may still be eligible, but should consult the IC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — degrees required
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates must have a clinical or research doctorate (examples: PhD, MD, DO, DDS/DMD, DVM/VMD, ScD, PharmD or equivalent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clinician-scientists (MD, DDS, DVM, nurses with research doctorates, etc.) are eligible; those needing longer mentored training should consider other K mechanisms (e.g., K08, K23).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals are NOT eligible if they have held an independent research or tenure-track faculty position, have more than 4 years of postdoctoral research training, have been independent PD/PI on NIH research grants or career development awards, or have led peer-reviewed research grants over $100,000 direct costs per year, or served as Project Leader on P01/P50 subprojects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These exclusions apply regardless of sector (academia, industry, etc.). Reviewers/institutions should document and confirm prior appointments and grant leadership roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence to document (non-)independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide documentation/evidence demonstrating non-independence or independence of the candidate's position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence for non-independence may include: candidate's research entirely funded by another investigator; research conducted in another investigator's assigned space; institutional policies preventing hiring staff or supervising students; inability to submit applications as PD/PI; lack of faculty privileges (e.g., faculty meetings). Evidence of independence includes full-time faculty appointment, start-up package, dedicated research space, rights to hire staff, eligibility to apply as PD/PI for NIH research funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citizenship and visa considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no citizenship requirement; candidates may be U.S. citizens, permanent residents, or non-U.S. citizens with appropriate visas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For K99 and R00 phases, the applicant and R00 institutions are responsible for documenting that visa status allows the candidate to remain in the U.S. long enough to complete the K99 phase and for the duration of the R00 award respectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Level of effort — K99 phase
rubrics_metrics.description: At time of award, candidates must have a full-time appointment and commit a minimum of 75% full-time professional effort (minimum 9 person-months) to the career development program; physician-scientists in surgical specialties may request minimum 50% effort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Candidates may engage in other duties during the remaining effort provided they do not detract from the career development program. VA appointments cannot be counted toward the applicant institution’s full-time requirement without consulting NIH staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Level of effort — R00 (independent) phase
rubrics_metrics.description: For the R00 phase, recipients must devote no less than 75% (9 person-months) of full-time, 12-month professional effort to research (50% for surgical specialties allowed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The required 9 person-months need not be devoted exclusively to R00-supported research, but teaching, clinical duties and other non-research activities should be minimal. R00 activation requires demonstration of protected research time by the sponsoring institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentor(s) qualifications and commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must identify a mentor who is an active investigator in the proposed research area and who is committed to the candidate's career development and direct supervision of research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentor must document availability of sufficient research support and facilities. Mentoring teams/advisory committees are encouraged; one primary mentor must coordinate the candidate’s research. For clinical doctorate candidates include at least one clinical-doctorate mentor. If primary mentor lacks mentoring experience, include a co-mentor with a strong track record. Mentor(s) should have successful track records mentoring similar career-stage individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional environment and commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant institution must have a strong, well-established record of research and career development activities and faculty qualified to serve as mentors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For R00 activation, the institution must provide protected research time (minimum 9 person-months), a start-up and salary package comparable to that for newly hired faculty without grants, and describe how the candidate's ability to apply for independent R01-level funding will be fostered. Institutions must confirm the appointment is tenure-track (or equivalent) and not contingent on transferring the award. NIH may review start-up packages and institutional commitments and can decline activation if inadequate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research plan and candidate career development plan content
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must include Candidate Information and Goals, Candidate Background, Career Goals and Objectives, and a tailored Plan for Career Development/Training Activities describing how mentored activities will lead to independence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present a scientific history showing progression from prior work to proposed mentored and independent phases and justify need for further mentored development. The career development plan should specify activities (research, grant-writing, communication, leadership, lab management) and how these will enhance research productivity and facilitate new approaches. Describe how skills obtained during K99 will enable independence and new research directions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation from mentor and path to independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how the candidate plans to separate scientifically from his/her mentor and advance to research independence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete plans and timelines; recipients are encouraged (but not required) to apply for independent positions at different institutions. If staying at mentored institution, provide a clear plan for separation and independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical trial policy for this NOFO
rubrics_metrics.description: Independent clinical trials, clinical trial feasibility studies, and ancillary clinical trials led by the candidate are not allowed under this NOFO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Candidates may propose to gain experience in a clinical trial led by a mentor or co-mentor as part of career development. Those proposing to lead clinical trials should apply to the companion NOFO (PA-24-193).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application form/content compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must follow the Career Development (K) Instructions in the How to Apply - Application Guide except where this NOFO provides different instructions; conformance is required and strictly enforced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Noncompliant applications may be delayed or not accepted for review. Follow page limits in the How to Apply - Application Guide and Table of Page Limits. Use specified forms (PHS 398 Career Development Award Supplemental Form components: Candidate, Research Plan, Other Candidate Information, Mentor(s), Environment & Institutional Commitment, Other Research Plan Sections, Appendix).

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget rules — general
rubrics_metrics.description: Award budgets consist of salary and program-related expenses; K99 budgets require itemized budget information per budget period, while R00 may request total amount per budget period with certain required entries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For R00 budget periods select Budget Type, provide period start/end dates; in Section A provide PD/PI entry with appropriate effort and $0 salary/fringe; in Section F add line item titled 'R00 Independent Phase' with the total request (up to $249,000). At transition, R00 institution must submit a detailed non-modular budget. Salary requested must be consistent with institutional salary structures and within legislated salary caps; additional compensation from other Federal sources allowed only if total Federal salary does not exceed cap and total percent effort ≤100%.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget rules — R00 total cost limit and indirect costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The total cost for the independent phase (R00) may not exceed $249,000 per year (includes salary, fringe, research costs, and applicable indirect costs). Indirect costs for K99 are reimbursed at 8% of modified total direct costs; for R00, indirect costs reimbursed at the extramural sponsoring institution’s indirect cost rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indirect costs requested by consortium participants are included in the total cost limitation. R00 institutions must negotiate and justify budgets; NIH Grants Policy Statement applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other program-related allowable expenses
rubrics_metrics.description: Participating ICs will provide research development support funds to be used for tuition/fees related to career development; research-related expenses (supplies, equipment, technical personnel); travel to meetings/training; statistical services including personnel and computer time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Salary for mentors, secretarial and administrative assistants is not allowed. See Table of IC-Specific Information for IC-specific programmatic/budgetary details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required registrations and institutional administrative readiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant organizations must complete SAM registration (including UEI/CAGE/NCAGE as applicable), eRA Commons registration, Grants.gov registration, and other registrations before submission; PD(s)/PI(s) must have eRA Commons accounts and link to ORCID.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrations can take 6 weeks or more; complete them well before the due date. eRA Commons requires identification of at least one Signing Official and at least one PD/PI account; PD/PI who is also SO must have two distinct eRA Commons accounts. ORCID must be linked to PD/PI eRA Commons profile.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application submission platforms
rubrics_metrics.description: Use NIH ASSIST, institutional system-to-system (S2S), or Grants.gov Workspace to prepare and submit applications; use eRA Commons to track application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check with institutional officials for system availability and timing; use the specified submission options to access forms. All applications are due by 5:00 PM local time of applicant organization; apply early to allow time for corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number and overlap of applications policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant organizations may submit more than one application provided each is scientifically distinct and from a different candidate; NIH will not accept duplicate or highly overlapping applications under review at the same time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An individual may not have two or more competing NIH career development applications pending concurrently. Rules prohibit A0/A1 overlap submissions prior to issuance of summary statements and applications substantially overlapping others under appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: R00 activation requirements and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: To activate the R00 phase, individuals must have been offered and accepted a tenure-track, full-time assistant professor position (or equivalent) by the end of the K99 project period; the R00 institution must demonstrate appropriate infrastructure and institutional commitment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients are encouraged to contact NIH program officials as soon as plans develop and not later than 6 months prior to K99 end. R00 application should be submitted no later than 2 months prior to proposed activation date. NIH will not activate R00 if institutional commitment (protected time, start-up, appointment, support for applying for R01) is inadequate.

rubrics_metrics.name: R00 application contents when requesting activation
rubrics_metrics.description: The R00 application must include a new signed face page, updated project description/abstract, detailed non-modular budget pages for each period, biosketches for PD/PI and key personnel, a Resources page, brief K99 progress description (Final Progress Report), an updated research plan (specific aims updated and described in <5 pages), updated human subjects/inclusion, authentication of key resources, vertebrate animals (if applicable), biohazards (if applicable), and a new checklist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two additional documents: a letter from the R00 Department/Division Chair describing institutional commitment to the candidate and plans for career development; and the final evaluation statement by the K99 mentor (if not already provided). Send original application plus one copy to the awarding IC's Grants Management contact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional start-up and use of R00 funds
rubrics_metrics.description: The R00 sponsoring institution must provide a start-up and salary package equivalent to that provided to newly hired tenure-track (or equivalent) faculty without grant support; R00 funds may not be used to offset typical startup packages or usual institutional salary commitments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe academic appointment details and confirm appointment is not contingent on transfer of the award. Institution must describe how recipient’s ability to apply for and secure R01-level support will be fostered. NIH may review start-up packages prior to activation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting and evaluation expectations post-award
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must submit annual RPPRs and financial statements; for mentored awards the Mentor’s Report must include an annual evaluation of the candidate’s progress. Final RPPR, invention statement, and expenditure data portion of the Federal Financial Report are required for closeout.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH may request information after award completion for program evaluation (employment history, publications, grants, honors). Follow Supplemental Instructions for Individual Career Development (K) RPPRs and NIH Grants Policy Statement reporting requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data management and sharing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: When applicable, award recipients must adhere to the 2023 NIH Policy for Data Management and Sharing and implement an approved Data Management and Sharing Plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the NIH Grants Policy Statement for details; applicants should include appropriate plans in application materials if data sharing is applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intramural-specific guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Mentored awards in the NIH intramural program will be supported by intramural funds; budget details and salary will be negotiated with the sponsoring intramural laboratory and consistent with intramural positions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: K99 recipients may apply for independent positions within the NIH IRP, but accepting an IRP position will not activate an R00 because intramural scientists are not eligible for NIH extramural grant awards.
